title: Memory-footprint smoothing for continuous KV batches
creator: Marta Chen
description:
Summary:
This ticket defines a concrete implementation for smoothing GPU memory footprint when serving continuous batching workloads that interact with a paged/blocked KV cache. The goal is to reduce p99 latency spikes caused by large simultaneous page faults during inflight batched requests while preserving batching efficiency and steady-state throughput.

Background and motivation:
- Continuous batching increases the number of concurrent inference contexts that reference KV cache slices. Under oversubscription, blocked/paged KV segments can cause coordinated GPU swaps resulting in multi-request stalls and p99 regressions.
- Prior designs focused on aggressive prefetching or coarse eviction policies, but both can either waste GPU memory or increase IO. We need a middle ground that smooths memory pressure across batch windows.

Design overview (approach):
1) Page-band windowing: instead of treating page fetches as instantaneous, introduce a small time-band (configurable, default 12ms) during which KV page loads are staggered across requests in the same continuous batch window. This reduces simultaneous PCIe/NVMe IO bursts.
2) Soft-reserve slots: maintain a light-weight per-shard quota of GPU resident slots (slot = fixed-size KV page); when a batch enters the system, it acquires soft-reserve tokens to pull hot pages. Tokens are replenished at a token-bucket rate aligned to expected batch arrival rate.
3) Adaptive prefetch hints: infer per-token affinity from recent request traces (hot prefixes) and only prefetch pages with an affinity score above a dynamic threshold. Threshold adapts based on recent swap latency and backend IO saturation.
4) Cooperative eviction grace period: evictions scheduled while a batch is in flight are deferred for a small grace period to avoid thrashing hot pages that will be immediately re-accessed.
5) Metrics and backpressure: integrate a lightweight backpressure signal to upstream router to temporarily reduce batch size or route to a lower-capacity pool if paging latency or IO queue length exceeds safety bounds.

Implementation details (data structures and algorithms):
- Block layout: pages are fixed 256KB blocks. Implement a compact resident-set bitmap per GPU slab (serialized as 64-bit words) to allow fast population count and contiguous-run detection for coalesced IO.
- Soft-reserve token-bucket: per-shard struct with current_tokens (int), refill_rate (tokens/sec), max_burst. Tokens are only requested heuristically and not guaranteed to be granted (soft semantics).
- Prefetch scoring: sliding window of 1s counts for prefix hits per page; score = alpha * recent_hits + beta * (recency_decay). Tune alpha/beta in experiments.
- Stagger scheduler: lightweight in-memory priority queue keyed by (batch_arrival_time + random_jitter_in_band). Use consistent hashing to ensure page fetches from the same host NVMe are not perfectly synchronized.
- Eviction policy: LRU-approximation with hotness decay; evictions mark pages as grace-protected for grace_period_ms.

Trade-offs considered:
- Aggressiveness of prefetch vs IO cost: we favor precision (higher threshold) to avoid excessive NVMe writes but allow operator override.
- Token-bucket conservatism: conservative defaults reduce peak IO but may reduce throughput for bursty tenants; provide per-customer override via Dedicated config.
- Grace period length: too long delays reclaiming cold pages; too short reintroduces thrash. We chose 12-50ms tuning range in experiments.

Testing plan and experiments performed:
- Microbenchmarks: simulated continuous arrival traces from internal production replay tool (~1M requests) across 3 models (gpt-small, gpt-medium, long-sequence). Measured p50/p95/p99 gen latency and NVMe IO throughput.
- Results (prod-like env, 4x A100s, NVMe 3GB/s): baseline (no smoothing) p99 = 920ms, with page-band windowing + soft-reserve p99 = 240ms, p95 reduced from 120ms to 60ms, steady-state throughput unchanged within 3%. IO spikes reduced by ~6x.
- Edge case: cold-start workloads with large unique contexts saw a ~9% increase in average token latency due to staggered fetch; mitigated by enabling higher prefetch threshold temporarily for cold sessions.

Compatibility and rollout plan:
- Feature gated: runtime flag kv.smoothing.enabled and per-customer override. Start with canary on internal infra, then narrow customer pilot (low-traffic Dedicated customers).
- Rollout phases: canary (1 week), small pilot (2 weeks), ramp to 25% traffic (2 weeks), full rollout conditional on metrics.
- Metrics to watch: p99 generation latency, NVMe queue depth, GPU utilization, request drop/backpressure events, token spend.

APIs and observability changes:
- New runtime metrics: kv.soft_reserve_tokens, kv.prefetch_score_histogram, kv.page_band_median_ms, kv.eviction_grace_count.
- Console dashboard: add KV paging panel with time-series for page fetch latency, IO throughput, and per-model p99.

Follow-ups and open questions:
- Should soft-reserve tokens be withdrawable across shards during skewed hotness? (Follow-up: ENG-xxxxxx research spike)
- Fine-grained per-customer tuning UX in Console.
- Investigate OS-level IO scheduler knobs and whether io_uring options can further reduce page fetch latency.

Acceptance criteria:
- p99 reduced >= 3x for production continuous batching traces compared to baseline in canary.
- No more than 5% regressive effect on p50 or throughput for cold-start workloads with default config.
- Observability dashboards show stable IO and page fetch patterns during a 2-week pilot.
comments: 2026-02-19: Initial spike created. Drafted the staggered page-band idea and token-bucket concept (Marta).
2026-02-24: Implementation spike: prototype of resident-set bitmap and ordered fetch queue in runtime branch. Preliminary microbenchmarks show 3.5x p99 improvement (Ethan). PR opened: runtime#4789.

2026-03-02: Design review with storage team: suggested using NVMe namespaces per-shard to reduce contention; decision: postpone per-namespace optimization to follow-up. (Notes attached to Confluence).
2026-03-07: Load test with 4x A100s on staging: observed reduced IO bursts but cold-start average latency increased ~9%; added adaptive prefetch threshold logic to address. (Ethan, Asha).
2026-03-10: Security reviewed: no customer data copied off-device; KMS unaffected. Marking security_review_required=false. (Security team approval).
2026-03-12: Canary rollout started for internal traffic. Monitoring dashboards added; p99 improved as expected. Next: pilot with two customers on Dedicated. (Marta).
